chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
“Regarding two spouts: one of them flowed with urine and the other with rainwater, then they mixed and it reached a man’s garment— that did not harm him.”

key_terms.بَوْلٌ: urine, treated here as an impurity
key_terms.فَاخْتَلَطَ: then the two liquids became mixed together
key_terms.لَمْ يَضُرَّهُ: it did not adversely affect him, meaning it did not make the garment problematic

ai.seo_question: If urine mixes with rainwater and splashes onto a garment, does it make the garment impure?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity when impure urine becomes mixed with rainwater. It indicates that in this case, if the mixture reaches a person’s garment, it does not render it problematic, reflecting the jurisprudential treatment of flowing rainwater in purification.
